summary: The article argues that deteriorating utility infrastructure is a leading cause of electricity, water and internet outages, citing incidents in Newford and Oldington. It surveys remedies including smart grids, quantum networking, city overhauls such as Broadville's, community-funded upgrades in Riverwood, new financing ideas, and engineering education. The central message is that proactive investment and anticipation are needed to reduce service interruptions.
one_line: Aging utility infrastructure causes outages worldwide, and proactive investment, new technology, financing strategies and education are presented as ways to prevent them.
key_facts: On September 15th, 2023, a major power outage in Newford left approximately 100,000 residents without power.
The Newford outage was caused by a transformer failure at a substation built over six decades ago.
Angela Hartwick, a local business owner, said her ice cream melted during the outage: "Every minute of power loss means lost revenue."

Dr. Samuel Clarkson, a civil engineer, said in an October 20th, 2023 interview that many power grids and water systems were installed in the post-war boom and were not designed for today's demands or a changing climate.
On November 4th, the city of Oldington in the UK had a major internet outage when old underground cables failed, disrupting remote work and online schooling for thousands.
Jane Fisher, a remote worker in Oldington, said it was the third outage of the year.
Smart grid technologies offer real-time monitoring and response that can isolate and manage outages, minimizing downtime.
Quantum networking is described as still in its infancy but could produce faster internet more resistant to infrastructure failures.
On December 1st, Mayor Laura Keegan announced a comprehensive infrastructure overhaul for Broadville to be completed by 2030.
Broadville's plan includes replacing aging pipes with corrosion-resistant materials and establishing redundant power systems.
Residents of Riverwood voted overwhelmingly on January 5th, 2024 to increase local taxes to fund utility infrastructure upgrades.
A summit on February 9th, 2024 discussed financing ideas such as green bonds, public-private partnerships, and incremental tariff increases.
Professor Elena Torres of the Metropolitan University's School of Engineering said on March 3rd that curricula must keep pace with technology to prepare students for future challenges.
